name: ApplianceLinc
description: The SwitchLinc, LampLinc and ApplianceLinc code base as used by the ApplianceLinc and other plug-in, outdoor and timer on/off modules.

operatingFlags.name: programmingLock
operatingFlags.label: Programming lock
operatingFlags.description: Linking and programming from the device itself are locked out.

operatingFlags.name: ledOnTransmit
operatingFlags.label: Blink LED when sending
operatingFlags.description: The status LED blinks when the device sends an Insteon message.

verification.note: The Insteon Developer's Guide reads bit 4 of the 0x00 reply as LED on, but later sources read it as LED off, the state 0x08 sets.

operatingFlags.name: loadSense
operatingFlags.label: Load sense
operatingFlags.description: Load sense is on: the device turns its load on when it senses the attached lamp or appliance being switched on.

operatingFlags.name: cleanupReport
operatingFlags.label: Send cleanup reports
operatingFlags.description: The device sends a success report after the cleanup messages that follow a group command. Only dealer firmware has this setting.

readings.name: databaseDelta
readings.label: ALL-Link database changes
readings.description: A count that goes up whenever the ALL-Link database changes.

values.name: x10HouseCode
values.label: X10 house code
values.description: The X10 house code, or 0x20 for no X10 address.

values.name: signalToNoiseLastFailure
values.label: Last signal-to-noise failure
values.description: The signal-to-noise value of the last failure.

standardCommands.name: lightOn
standardCommands.description: Turns the load on. The device doesn't read cmd2; send 0xFF.

standardCommands.name: readStatus
standardCommands.description: Reads whether the load is on. The acknowledgment's cmd1 carries the ALL-Link database delta.

responder.name: onLevel
responder.label: On or off
responder.description: 0x00 turns the load off when the controller's On arrives, 0xFF on.

verification.note: Read from the On/Off Outlet and On/Off Module, Dual-Band Developer Notes, which give Data 1 as the on-level; no document describes this product's records. Inferred: seen on two i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48) linked to a Hub 2245, the device itself writes its responder record when it's linked remotely or with the SET button, and takes Data 1 from the load's state at that moment: the two plugs wrote 0x00 when the load was off and 0xFF when it was on. The On/Off Plug 2635-222 Owner's Manual says to make sure the module is on before linking it as a responder; the On/Off Module 2456S3 Owner's Manual and the Outdoor On/Off Module 2456S3E Owner's Manual say to set the load to the state the link should recall before linking it as a responder. The values given here are what to write when writing the record by hand.
No document says that every nonzero level means on; the ranges are read from Light Status Request's level byte (cmd2), as the Insteon Developer's Guide describes it for on/off devices.

No document says whether this relay holds the state a command switches it to. It follows from the command set: none of its operating flags or flag commands is a momentary or pulse setting, so no flag makes the relay return to off by itself.

notes: The Insteon Developer's Guide lists 0x0A and above as unused on this code base; later sources add the cleanup report commands 0x0A and 0x0B.
Earlier sources give D12 as the signal-to-noise ratio and D13 as a count of messages with CRC errors.

valueTables.name: onOff
valueTables.description: Off and on, for a load or LED a record switches.
